title: Reconnectable single-terminal protocol message contract
source_of_truth: docs/adr/sandbox-lifecycle.md (Proposed, 2026-09-22): section 1 detach semantics, section 3 unified entry and state gate
docs/adr/runner-language.md (Accepted, 2026-09-21): CLI goes through the control plane, never the Runner directly
issue #13: acceptance criteria and the 2026-10-02 scoping note (contract may proceed in parallel to #76; closes only with runtime integration)

open_decisions.question: serve the terminal via ttyd in front of tmux, or own the PTY/WebSocket bridge
open_decisions.resolution_home: runtime integration under #13; decision criteria listed in docs/contracts/terminal-protocol.md
open_decisions.contract_independence: either backend speaks the same JSON frames defined here; the backend choice must not leak into the frame table

transport.binding: JSON text frames over a single WebSocket connection per terminal attachment
transport.entry: the unified console.<domain> entry per ADR sandbox-lifecycle.md section 3; the CLI never calls the Runner directly
transport.backend: ttyd or an owned PTY bridge is the OPEN decision in open_decisions; the frames are identical either way
transport.bounds: max frame size and max input/output data byte size, like the server buffer size, are set at runtime integration under #13; rate_limited deferral follows the same runtime bounds

common_fields.seq: integer, per-direction monotonic counter on the connection; gaps on the server side are allowed after output drops
common_fields.ts: integer, Unix epoch milliseconds on the sender clock

frames.name: hello
frames.purpose: authenticate and attach to one sandbox terminal

field_notes.token: control-plane session token from #12; never the Claude API key; must not appear in logs
field_notes.generation: generation the client last saw from GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}; omitted when unknown

frames.name: hello_ack
frames.purpose: confirm the attach and state the live identity and applied size

field_notes.generation: the generation this connection is bound to; every later frame on the connection is fenced by it
field_notes.cols: size actually applied to the tmux session under last_resize_wins
field_notes.rows: size actually applied to the tmux session under last_resize_wins
field_notes.replay_follows: when true, the next output frame has origin replay with the captured current screen

field_notes.code: one of the closed error_codes set valid at hello time
field_notes.message: human-readable, safe for logs, no secrets

frames.name: input
frames.purpose: send user keystrokes to the PTY

field_notes.data: UTF-8 text; control keys ride as raw bytes (Ctrl-C is the byte 0x03); the server never interprets, filters, or translates them

frames.name: output
frames.purpose: stream terminal output to the client

field_notes.data: UTF-8 stream text with ANSI escape sequences passed through unmodified
field_notes.origin: live (default) or replay (current-screen capture sent after attach or resync)
field_notes.code: only output_limit_exceeded: the drop-to-sync notice; data is empty when code is set

field_notes.cols: integer 1..500; outside the bounds is invalid_frame
field_notes.rows: integer 1..500; outside the bounds is invalid_frame

frames.name: resized
frames.purpose: tell every attached window the size that was actually applied

field_notes.source: self, peer, or server: which side caused the applied size

field_notes.note: counted as liveness, never as user activity

field_notes.code: error_codes entry when the end is an error condition, else absent

error_codes.client_action: obtain a fresh control-plane token and reconnect
unknown, destroyed, or another tenant's sandbox; no retry against the same id
request Active via POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/state and attach after the operation succeeds
execution instance was recreated; re-read GET /v1/sandboxes/{id} and attach fresh to the current generation
dropped output exceeded the recovery cap while in drop_to_sync; reconnect is allowed and the screen is restored from capture
drop-to-sync notice: queued output was discarded; any client frame exits the mode and triggers a capture replay
schema violation such as an unknown type, bad fields, or resize outside bounds; fix the client
frame rate above the per-connection limit; reconnect with backoff

reconnect.screen_replay: on a successful attach the server sends output frames with origin replay holding a tmux capture of the current visible screen, then live output
reconnect.no_content_buffer: there is no server-side terminal content buffer in any form; replay is always a fresh capture of what is on the screen now
reconnect.cold_resume: after cold suspend and resume the processes are new; the replay shows the new session screen, not the old one (ADR sandbox-lifecycle.md section 1)

size_policy.status: Proposed: explicit two-window decision tracked by #13

behavior: each accepted resize frame is applied to the tmux session as the new size
every attached connection receives a resized notification with the applied cols and rows
an older window does not veto a newer resize; its local rendering adapts on the notification

input_passthrough.statement: input data is UTF-8 text; control keys ride as raw bytes (Ctrl-C is the byte 0x03) and the server never interprets, filters, or translates them; the PTY/tmux session turns bytes into signals
input_passthrough.ctrl_c: the server must not synthesize SIGINT on its own; Ctrl-C reaches the program only as the byte the client sent

output_passthrough.statement: output data is UTF-8 stream text; ANSI escape sequences pass through unmodified; the server never parses, filters, or alters output
output_passthrough.storage: terminal content is forwarded and discarded; only numeric frame and byte counters survive (activity_classification.counters)

activity_classification.purpose: the idle policy in #19 and ops dashboards in #23 must tell real user activity apart from liveness, layout, and server traffic

counters.user_input_frames: per sandbox, incremented once per input frame
counters.user_input_bytes: per sandbox, sum of bytes in input frame data
counters.output_frames: per sandbox, incremented once per output frame; separate from the input counters
counters.output_bytes: per sandbox, sum of bytes in output frame data; a number only, never content

lifecycle_binding.binding: a connection is bound to sandbox_id + generation at hello time; hello is the first client frame, and any other frame arriving before hello_ack is answered with bye code invalid_frame; every frame after hello_ack is fenced by that identity

on_stop_or_destroy.rule: when the sandbox moves to Suspending or Destroying the server sends bye and only then closes the WebSocket; bye is always the final server frame

detach.statement: a client bye or a dropped WebSocket never kills the tmux session or its processes; only the attachment goes away

reconnect_after_destroy.note: destroyed, unknown, and cross-tenant ids all answer with the same code; no probe signal

wrong_generation_guard.client_action: re-read GET /v1/sandboxes/{id} and attach fresh to the current generation; the fresh attach replays the new screen

not_active.note: any observed_state outside Active and Idle, including Suspend, answers at hello; the client asks for Active through the state endpoint and attaches after the operation succeeds (ADR sandbox-lifecycle.md section 3)

buffer.size_bytes: set at runtime integration under #13; must be finite and explicit, never unbounded

actions: discard every queued output frame; count the discarded span in dropped_bytes (numeric counter only, content is not kept)
send exactly one output frame with code output_limit_exceeded and empty data
keep counting newly produced output in dropped_bytes while the mode is active

backpressure.exit_drop_to_sync: the first client frame after the notice (input, resize, or ping) proves the client is alive; the server sends one output frame with origin replay holding a tmux capture of the current visible screen and resumes live forwarding

fatal_cap.condition: dropped_bytes exceeds the per-connection recovery cap
fatal_cap.action: server sends bye with code backpressure_overflow, then closes; reconnect is allowed

related_tickets.role: owner: protocol acceptance checkboxes and runtime integration
parallel API/terminal ticket boundary; this contract proceeds independently
idle policy consumes the user_input activity class
ops consumes the activity classes and byte counters
control-plane API and session token fields used at hello
